name: APT29 C2 1 - HTTP Beacons with Jitter to a Loopback Server (T1071.001)
blast_radius: Runs a loopback-only HTTP server in an in-process runspace and sends five POST beacons about two seconds apart with an uncommon user agent. No traffic leaves the host.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 3: connections to 127.0.0.1 on the beacon port
detection: NDR/EDR: periodic POSTs with a fixed body shape and unusual user agent

name: APT29 C2 2 - Generated Name Burst (T1568)
blast_radius: Resolves twelve generated base32 names under .invalid in quick succession from the PowerShell process. Queries go to the host resolver and cannot resolve.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 22: DNS queries for the generated names
detection: DNS analytics: burst of high-entropy NXDOMAIN lookups from one process

name: APT29 C2 3 - Local Port Proxy Configured, Used Once and Removed (T1090.001)
blast_radius: Gated by BAS_CONFIRM_APT29_PORTPROXY=true (exact) and administrator only. Adds a netsh port proxy from a random loopback port to the next one, connects through it once and deletes only its own rule. Existing port proxy rules are never touched.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 1: netsh.exe interface portproxy add
detection: EDR: netsh portproxy add by a script host
cleanup:
Get-ChildItem -Path $env:TEMP -Filter 'bas_a29_*' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
(netsh interface portproxy show v4tov4 | Out-String) -split [Environment]::NewLine | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match '^\s*127\.0\.0\.1\s+(4\d{4})\s+127\.0\.0\.1\s+(4\d{4})\s*$') { & netsh interface portproxy delete v4tov4 listenport=$($matches[1]) listenaddress=127.0.0.1 | Out-Null } }
